paper_sections.title: Correlations between cross-classification accuracy and subjective rating

description.value: An fMRI study used the rubber hand illusion and multivoxel pattern analysis to investigate supramodal neural representations of body ownership across visuotactile and visuomotor modalities.

description.value: A two-by-two within-subject factorial fMRI experiment manipulated modality and timing of visual feedback; an independent EBA functional localizer was performed afterward.

spans.text: Third, the analysis revealed significant above-chance classification accuracies in the right PMv, the left EBA, and the bilateral IPS in cross-classification between visuotactile and visuomotor sessions.

value: Significant above-chance cross-classification accuracy was observed in the right PMv, left EBA, and bilateral IPS, indicating neural representations invariant to the sensory modalities.

spans.text: Our results provide further insight and reveal a supramodal signature of the sense of body ownership across the sensory modalities in the EBA.

description.value: A sphere with a radius of 5 mm centered on MNI coordinates [−48, −70, 8] for the left hemisphere and [51, −58, 2] for the right hemisphere.
Participants received tactile stimulation or executed finger movements while viewing synchronous or asynchronous videos of their right hand.

spans.text: Participants received tactile stimulation or executed finger movements while given synchronous and asynchronous visual feedback of their hand.

The video presentation was implemented by Computer Vision Toolbox (  https://mathworks.com/products/computer-vision.html  ), Image Processing Toolbox (  https://mathworks.com/products/image.html  ), MATLAB Support Package for USB Webcams (  https://mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/45182-matlab-support-package-for-usb-webcams  ), and Psychtoolbox (  http://psychtoolbox.org/  ) for MATLAB.

instructions.value: Participants lifted and lowered their right index finger in the visuomotor condition and attended to the visual feedback; they responded to questionnaire items after scanning.

stimuli.value: Videos of the participant's right hand; tactile brush stimulation and finger movements.

spans.text: In the visuotactile sessions, tactile stimulation was delivered by an experimenter manually with a paintbrush at a frequency of ∼1 Hz during 18 s, as cued by a beep.

description.value: Participants viewed blocks of headless human body-part images and chair images and performed a one-back repetition detection task.

spans.text: A body block consisted of 20 images of headless human body parts in different postures, which were alternated with a control block consisting of 20 images of chairs.
A total of 16 blocks were performed, which consisted of 8 body blocks and 8 control blocks.
The stimuli presentation was implemented by PsychoPy ( Peirce et al., 2019 ).

instructions.value: Participants pressed a button when they detected immediate repetitions.

spans.text: The participants were asked to press a button with the right index finger when they detected the immediate repetitions.

stimuli.value: Grayscale images of headless human body parts and chairs.
